subject: Technical deep dive recap: latency/throughput SLOs & deployment topology
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Technical deep dive recap: latency/throughput SLOs & deployment topology

Sarah — thanks for the deep dive earlier today. Quick recap so we’re aligned and to capture next steps. Please reply with any corrections.

Key pain points you shared:
- User-facing latency spikes during peak load (customer chat) causing poor UX and dropped sessions.
- Unpredictable cost growth as model usage scales.
- Need for strict data separation and auditability for regulated data.

Goals you outlined
- 95th percentile tail latency <= 250ms for short completions (<=64 tokens).
- Sustained throughput target of ~500 reqs/sec for chat workload; ability to burst to 1k reqs/sec for ~15 minutes.
- Multi-region failover (primary in us-west, failover in us-east) with RTO <= 5 minutes.
- Audit logs and KMS integration for sensitive models.

Model & workload constraints
- Primary model candidate: Llama-2-70B-client-tuned (we discussed quantized variants).
- Typical prompt + response size: 256 tokens total on average; 95th percentile under 512 tokens.
- Latency targets assume caching for repeated prefixes and batching where feasible.

Proposed deployment topology (high-level)
- Redwood Dedicated (private VPC) in your cloud account with a two-region setup (us-west primary, us-east hot-standby).
- Autoscaling GPU pools with pre-warmed capacity for expected burst windows + optional burst capacity to shared pool.
- Long-lived KV cache for session state (prefix caching) colocated with primary region to keep tail latency down.
- Canary rollout for model updates, automatic fallback to a smaller/cheaper variant under sustained capacity pressure.

Performance & reliability knobs we recommended
- Continuous batching with latency SLO-aware limits (max batch delay 10ms for interactive requests).
- Token-level throttling for heavy background jobs to protect customer-facing traffic.
- Quantized model profiles (int8/4) to balance cost vs. latency; we'll run perf benches on your representative prompts.

Attachments included:
- acme-slo-proposal.pdf (SLO targets and suggested validation tests)
- acme-network-diagram.png (proposed VPC/peering setup)

Next steps (owners & dates)
- Marissa: schedule kickoff & share test prompt set and benchmark harness — by Wed 7/22.
- Mateo: draft cost estimate & reserved capacity sizing for 500 reqs/sec sustained with burst profile — by Fri 7/24.
- Dylan: prepare deployment diagram and networking checklist for your security team (firewalls, peering, KMS) — by Fri 7/24.
- Sarah/Raj: confirm representative traffic patterns and provide any security questionnaire items you want us to prioritize.

If that all looks right I’ll schedule a 60-minute technical kickoff next week to walk through the benchmarking plan and instrumentation.

—
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks Marissa — this matches my notes and captures the ask well. A couple quick clarifications from our side:

1) Bursting: when you say "burst to 1k reqs/sec for ~15 minutes", can you call out what that looks like from a cost and warm-start perspective (i.e., how much pre-warm vs on-demand)?
2) Fallback behavior: for automatic fallback to smaller model variants, what quality degradation should we expect? Can you point to any evals you use for that comparison?
3) Security: our infra team will want the full networking diagram (we only saw the high-level one in the call). Could you attach a slightly higher-fidelity diagram for peering and firewall rules?

We’ll also pull together a short dump of representative traffic shapes and a few example prompts by EOD tomorrow.

On scheduling — a kickoff next Wed (7/29) 10–11am PT would work for us.

Thanks —

Sarah / Raj — great, thanks for the quick reply and for confirming availability for 7/29 10–11am PT.

Quick answers to your questions:
- Burst capacity: we'll include two cost scenarios in Mateo's estimate — (A) pre-warm 20% of peak to meet initial ramp with on-demand scaling for the remainder; (B) pre-warm 50% to minimize cold-starts during known high-traffic windows. We’ll highlight the warm-start latency delta for both.
- Fallback quality: Dylan will include a short evaluation doc showing expected metric deltas (response time, token-level perplexity proxies) between the full model and a quantized/smaller variant across your prompt set. Early expectation: small SxS quality regressions on edge cases; we’ll prioritize maintaining top-line intent accuracy.
- Networking diagram: attached is a higher-fidelity PNG and the SLO proposal PDF. Dylan, please confirm the firewall/peering checklist is complete for ACME’s security review.
